source.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Bangla recognizer, class 48 (ঁ, chandrabindu; user manual Table 4): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Bengali writers (MIT licence, 2012)
source.variation: The recognizer stores native Bengali writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 190 of the 194 stored prototypes of the chandrabindu are two pen-down strokes: the bowl first, then the dot. 178 of those 190 start the bowl on the left, 182 turn it counterclockwise (down, round and up), and 173 end it on the right; 180 place the dot within the bowl's width. The traces do not settle which way the dot is turned, so the path makes no claim about it and draws it as a short touch. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the order, the turning and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Bengali outline. Handwriting varies by writer.

source.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Bangla recognizer, class 47 (ঃ, bisarga; user manual Table 4): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Bengali writers (MIT licence, 2012)
source.variation: The recognizer stores native Bengali writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. All 195 stored prototypes of the bisarga are two pen-down strokes: the upper loop first (193) and the lower loop second (193). 171 begin the upper loop near its top. 151 of the upper loops and 152 of the lower ones turn counterclockwise, the rest clockwise, so the path takes the majority direction for both. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the order, the turning and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Bengali outline. Handwriting varies by writer.

source.variation: The recognizer stores native Bengali writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 194 of the 226 stored prototypes of the independent e are one pen-down stroke. 189 of those 194 start in the upper half, inside the small curl, and all 194 turn clockwise: round the curl, over the arch and down the right side. 190 end on the left, at the top of the hook, so the base is swept from right to left. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the order, the turning and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Bengali outline. Handwriting varies by writer.

source.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Bangla recognizer, class 12 (খ, kha; user manual Table 4): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Bengali writers (MIT licence, 2012)
source.variation: The recognizer stores native Bengali writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 189 of the 212 stored prototypes of kha are one pen-down stroke. 179 of those 189 start on the left, in the curl, and in 169 the curl turns counterclockwise. The stroke then crosses the middle, comes down to the pointed left tip, rounds the lower curve and climbs the stem: 185 end at the top right, and 128 finish with a short move to the right, the flag beside the top of the stem. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the order, the turning and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Bengali outline. Handwriting varies by writer.

The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the order, the turning and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Bengali outline. Handwriting varies by writer.

source.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Bangla recognizer, class 33 (ব, ba; user manual Table 4): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Bengali writers (MIT licence, 2012)
source.variation: The recognizer stores native Bengali writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 433 of the 477 stored prototypes of ba are one pen-down stroke. 258 of those 433 open with the headline, drawn left to right; most of the rest (86) draw no headline run at all. 308 start at the upper left, 350 finish by climbing the stem, and 393 end at the top right. The path keeps that order: the headline left to right, the turn into the stem and down the diagonal to the pointed left tip, the lower curve to the stem's foot, and the climb back up the stem. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the order, the turning and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Bengali outline. Handwriting varies by writer.
